subject: Regional routing fallback notice and action plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@brightpay.com>; BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: routing fallback guidance & customer action (BrightPay)

Hi Alyssa / BrightPay team,

I wanted to reach out directly with an operational note after the morning disruption that affected inference traffic coming from our US and EU edge POPs and intermittent behavior in APAC. Our engineering team detected a regional control-plane regression in the provider fabric that caused some requests to be queued and occasionally fail to route to the nearest region.

What to do now (short actionable steps):
- Switch client routing to the global fallback endpoint we exposed at: api.redwood.com/fallback (no config change for standard SDKs; see note below).
- If you have region pins, temporarily remove strict region pinning until 11:59 PT tonight to allow traffic to flow through the fallback.
- For synchronous latency-sensitive paths: add client-side retry with exponential backoff (start 100ms, max 1s) and cap total attempts to 3.

Our immediate mitigation is live: we’ve enabled a cross-region proxy that will route requests around the affected POPs. This will increase p95 latency by ~50-120ms for some calls for the next 6–12 hours; we estimated cost impact in the attached CSV.

I’ll keep you updated in this thread. If you want a brief call to walk through the temporary changes and implications for SLA, Marissa (CS) and I are available this afternoon.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: routing fallback guidance & customer action (BrightPay)

Adding technical context for the thread and confirming the mitigation steps Rachel outlined.

Timeline & root cause (brief):
- 08:41 PT: control-plane deployment to a peering daemon rolled back route advertisements in two US POPs and one EU POP due to an unexpected health-check change.
- 08:44 PT: we observed cascading rebalancing which caused temporary route thrashing and stale KV caches on some sidecars.
- 08:49 PT: automated rollback initiated, but a minority of connections persisted with degraded routing until the fallback proxy was enabled.

Mitigations in place:
- Cross-region proxy enabled at 09:05 PT (traffic now redirected away from affected POPs).
- Automatic KV cache invalidation job triggered for affected pools.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds temporarily relaxed to prevent client-level cascades.

What customers will see:
- Slightly higher median p95 latency for non-cached requests.
- No token loss; all requests are being served.

Next steps we are executing:
- Validate global autoscaling edges and run a smoke test across EU and APAC at 11:00 PT.
- Prepare a postmortem and an engineering remediation plan (will share draft shorty).

If BrightPay needs a deep-dive, I can join the call with our SREs.

—Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime
[Attachment referenced: customer-impact-times.csv (csv, 45KB)]

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the quick note and clear steps. A couple quick questions on our end:

1) Will enabling the fallback endpoint impact any of the rate limits on our account or change quota usage accounting?
2) Do you have an ETA for when strict region pinning can be safely re-applied? Our compliance team requires region pinning for certain workloads.

Also, can we get a short window where we can test failover before you revert changes? Late afternoon Pacific would be best for our SREs.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Head of Platform, BrightPay

Subject: RE: Immediate: routing fallback guidance & customer action (BrightPay)

Alyssa — quick answers and next actions below.

1) Quotas & rate limits: routing through the fallback endpoint does not change quota buckets or per-token billing. Because traffic may traverse additional hops, there is a small incremental compute cost on our side — we captured that in the attached CSV. You will not see double-charges or separate quota consumption.

2) Region pin re-application: engineering expects to re-enable strict region pinning after the validation smoke tests complete and the control-plane patch is rolled at 18:30 PT tonight. We’ll confirm in this thread when patches are complete.

Test window: we can schedule a 30-minute failover window at 16:30 PT today (31 Jul). Vivek / SREs will be on the call to monitor logs and KV cache state. Please confirm if that time works; I’ve included a short checklist below for the window.

Failover test checklist for BrightPay SREs:
- Run a small batch of inference calls targeting the EU region (10–20 requests) and verify sequence integrity.
- Observe p95 over 5 minutes and capture traces if any error codes (429/503) appear.
- Share a short snippet of client logs showing retry behavior.

Attachments: draft postmortem (rdx-4689-postmortem-draft.pdf) is attached. This is an engineering-first draft — we will produce a customer-facing postmortem once we finalize root cause details and remediation timelines.

Thanks for the quick coordination.

Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
